# Spot facts: sourced values and what is still unknown

Generated by `node --experimental-strip-types docs/forecast/data/build-spot-review.ts` from `src/ocean/spotProfiles.ts`. **Do not edit by hand.**

**What this is.** Every value below was read from a published source (or, for one facing, Pismo’s, derived from CDIP agency data) (user decision, 2026-11-02: look at public sources and apply them) and carries its URL and retrieval date. The pages were read through page summaries by automated fetch tools, NOT verified against the full pages, and none of it is surveyed or reviewed by a person. Spot-guide facts (facing, swell range, tide, bottom, size, hazards) come from Surfnerd and Surf-Forecast.com spot guides (T-073 adds Wannasurf and The Surf Atlas) and are labelled provenance “published guide”; where no guide states a single facing, the facing may be derived from coastline geometry (CDIP MOP shore normals) and is labelled “derived from coastline geometry”; the minimum swell period is a generic published threshold, not specific to the spot. A review is optional: tick “change to” on any row to replace a value. Where the guides disagree, the narrower swell window and the more cautious exposure word are used and the disagreement is in the note. A spot gets a surf estimate only if it has a facing and a swell range (points, reefs and jetties also need a source that says exposed); a spot a source calls sheltered estimates only through its CDIP nearshore point (never the offshore-swell v1) and only inside the swell directions a guide lists it as open to, and a spot whose published working swell wraps onto it from outside ±60° of its facing refuses (T-073, docs/forecast/ESTIMATE-COVERAGE-T073.md); the rating rules are unchanged. One side effect to know about: a published facing lets the rating tell offshore from onshore wind at the spots that now have one (39 instead of 1 at T-071, 44 at T-073), so ratings there shifted: across all spots in daylight hours, SOLID or better went from 9.1% to 20.7% of spot-hours (docs/forecast/ESTIMATE-COVERAGE-T071.md).

Where no source states a fact, the row says “none found” and the fact stays unknown.

It sits in a big bay just beyond Backyards, in the shadow of Phantom Reef, which focuses incoming swell into the bay and funnels it onto V-Land's shallow, uneven lava ledge. It breaks over uneven, often shallow and sharp reef across an elbow, throwing up both a left and a right. The right is faster but shorter and draws very shallow on the inside, while the bonus left off the middle runs shoulderier and more forgiving as it spills into deeper water. Its three sections, the outside, middle, and bowl, each offer roll-ins, workable walls, and the odd tube, and it can turn hollow and fast when it's on. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner. From shoulder to overhead it stays within reach of experienced surfers, but as the size climbs it turns increasingly heavy and twisted. Way outside sits Outer Log Cabins, a notorious tow-in reef that has held some of the biggest waves ever ridden. Skill (surfnerd): Expert. Surfnerd overview: Ala Moana Bowls is one of the best waves on Oahu, a long, barreling reef that peels outside the Ala Wai Harbor. It owes its shape to dredging: a deepwater channel was cut so boats could reach the harbour, and south swell refracts out of that channel and wedges up along the reef. Expect big, round curves as the wave bowls over sections of reef, shoulders off, then gathers into another barrel on the shallow inside. It breaks both left and right over live coral. Surfnerd has 2 entries for this break with different stated facings (ala-moana-bowls=SSW, ala-moana-bowls-hawaii=SW); seaward uses the primary entry (ala-moana-bowls), both kept. | Hazards | [\It throws up both lefts and rights, and it's aptly named: the crowds of anglers it draws also bring sharks, and the paddle out runs a long 200 yards.\ (surfnerd),\It breaks on all tides, but coming in off low is the easiest to handle for the rips, and a rising tide is generally the better call.\ (surfnerd),\One thing to plan for: the outgoing tide from the inlet keeps running out into the lineup for about an hour and a half after low tide on the beach, so you'll be paddling against a fast current the whole time.\ (surfnerd),\The lineup is only sometimes crowded, and when it's on, the long rides, changing sections, and strong rips spread everyone out; now and then waves break with nobody out, because few want to sit that far offshore on their own.\ (surfnerd),\Hazards include rips, locals, sharks,jetskis,sea-lice in Summer.\ (surf-forecast)] (sourced) | — | [Surfnerd spot guide: Monster Hole](https://www.surfnerd.com/surf-forecast/monster-hole) (retrieved 2026-11-09)<br>[Surf-Forecast.com spot guide: Monster Hole](https://www.surf-forecast.com/breaks/Monster-Hole) (retrieved 2026-11-09)<br>*From the guides; not a complete hazard list.* | Already sourced: ☐ confirm ☐ change to: ____ |

| Hazards | [\One quirk sets it apart from the area's other rocky breaks: instead of outcroppings limited to the first 20 feet of shoreline, it has a longer, more treacherous stretch of rock.\ (surfnerd),\Tide also changes how the rocks play: at low tide you can see where you're going, but at high tide the outcroppings turn into a toe-mangling minefield, so step carefully and watch your shins, feet and fins.\ (surfnerd),\Paddling out is not too bad most days but gets more challenging as the surf builds, and the rocks set up strange currents that can hold you stationary even on surprisingly small days.\ (surfnerd)] (sourced) | — | [Surfnerd spot guide: The Radisson](https://www.surfnerd.com/surf-forecast/the-radisson) (retrieved 2026-11-09)<br>*From the guides; not a complete hazard list.* | Already sourced: ☐ confirm ☐ change to: ____ |

When a solid northeast swell lines up with offshore winds from a passing front, it's one of the best spots on the Windward Side, with long rides and barrels, though catching it that good isn't all that common. Surfnerd overview: Kahului Harbor sits on the north-central coast of Maui and is a genuinely fun place to score, with several breaks firing inside and outside the harbor. The standout is the right on the west side. When a large swell pushes through the wide entrance, energy refracts out of the deeper channel and crosses up with swell bouncing off the jetty, stacking into a powerful roll-in wedge over shallow water. It is a mini-Box-style wedge that rewards surfers and bodyboarders who can handle abrupt steps and throw into barrels. There is a left off the same peak, but it dumps straight into the deep channel and does not offer much. Treat it as more of a novelty than a world-beater, though it is a blast when it turns on. Around the other side of the headland there's a second lefthander, but the water here is spooky, with a reputation for tiger sharks. A handful of other spots work nearby along the coast. Surfnerd overview: Pohoiki is a lava-reef spot with three separate bays, each offering a different wave over an uneven reef. The bottom is extremely sharp lava rock dotted with urchins, so it pays to avoid contact at all times. The three bays give you options. First Bay sits closest to the boat ramp, with a wave that suits all levels and warm water from nearby volcanic springs. Second Bay lies a little further out in slightly cooler water and throws a more hollow, faster wave for advanced surfers. Third Bay, around a small rocky outcrop to the south, is hollow and fast over shallow water, and can turn into a solid big-wave spot when a strong swell meets west-to-north wind. Surfnerd overview: Sandy Beach is a punishing beach break that throws its waves over sand. This is a neck-breaking shorebreak, one for talented, committed bodyboarders and bodysurfers who can handle a heavy pounding on any east-to-south swell. If you're on a board, your best option is to paddle outside to the shallow left reef, though it's usually blown to pieces by the trades. | Hazards | [\When conditions are clean it fires as a thick, right-hand reefbreak; on smaller days it drops into a peaky, rocky beachbreak.\ (surfnerd),\The reef sits in front of a creek mouth and is clogged with seaweed and boils, yet it still throws a decent right that peaks on the outside, backs off, then reforms and bowls into the inside section.\ (surfnerd),\When it's smaller, walk south of the short staircase to a wide beachbreak dotted with boulders and shallow reef, which comes into its own through summer but turns unsurfable once it's more than a few feet overhead.\ (surfnerd),\Expect a busy but friendly lineup when it's on, and be polite in the water, since there's a local presence alongside resident elephant seals and sharks in the area.\ (surfnerd)] (sourced) | — | [Surfnerd spot guide: Piedras Blancas](https://www.surfnerd.com/surf-forecast/piedras-blancas) (retrieved 2026-11-09)<br>*From the guides; not a complete hazard list.* | Already sourced: ☐ confirm ☐ change to: ____ |

| Hazards | [\Shark Pit sits way offshore at the mouth of Tomales Bay in Marin, where a left-hand barrel peels over a sandbar shaped by the river mouth.\ (surfnerd),\A rising tide is the call here, since the incoming push keeps the strong seaward currents at the river mouth in check.\ (surfnerd),\This is an experts-only wave, and not only because of the size and the currents.\ (surfnerd),\These are exceptionally dangerous waters: the area is a known great white breeding ground, with an attack on a surfer or diver roughly every couple of years.\ (surfnerd),\Shark Pit _1 in SF Marin is an exposed beach break that has reasonably consistent surf The best wind direction is from the east southeast with some shelter here from north winds.\ (surf-forecast),\Watch out for sharks, rips and rocks.\ (surf-forecast)] (sourced) | — | [Surfnerd spot guide: Shark Pit - Marin](https://www.surfnerd.com/surf-forecast/shark-pit-marin) (retrieved 2026-11-09)<br>[Surf-Forecast.com spot guide: Shark Pit - Marin](https://www.surf-forecast.com/breaks/Shark-Pit_1) (retrieved 2026-11-09)<br>*From the guides; not a complete hazard list.* | Already sourced: ☐ confirm ☐ change to: ____ |
